question: Under MREC Rule 3.2(G), how long must a Mississippi real estate broker keep on file complete records relating to a real estate transaction?
choice_a: One year following the listing date
choice_b: Three years following consummation of the transaction
choice_c: Five years following the closing date
choice_d: Seven years following termination of the listing agreement
explanation: MREC Rule 3.2(G) (Part 1601, Chapter 3, Administration/Conducting Business) requires a broker to keep on file for three years following consummation of a real estate transaction complete records relating to it, including listings, options, leases, offers to purchase, contracts of sale, escrow records, agency agreements, and copies of all closing statements. This three-year window runs from consummation, not from the listing date.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Part 1601, Ch. 3, Rule 3.2(G); Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-35

question: Which of the following is NOT explicitly listed among the transaction records a Mississippi broker must retain under Rule 3.2(G)?
choice_a: Escrow records
choice_b: Copies of all closing statements
choice_c: Federal income tax returns of the parties
choice_d: Agency agreements
explanation: Rule 3.2(G) requires retention of listings, options, leases, offers to purchase, contracts of sale, escrow records, agency agreements, and copies of closing statements. The tax returns of the transaction's buyer or seller are private financial documents of those parties and are not part of the broker's required retained transaction file.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Part 1601, Ch. 3, Rule 3.2(G)

question: Under MREC Rule 3.4(C), when is a broker's escrow account subject to inspection by the Commission?
choice_a: Only during a formal disciplinary hearing
choice_b: Only once per year during license renewal
choice_c: Only upon a court order
choice_d: At all times
explanation: Rule 3.4(C) states that escrow records must be kept in accordance with standard accounting practices and 'shall be subject to inspection at all times by the Commission.' This grants MREC ongoing audit access to trust account records, not access limited to hearings, renewal cycles, or court intervention.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Part 1601, Ch. 3, Rule 3.4(C)

question: When must a real estate licensee deliver a true and correct copy of an instrument to a party executing it?
choice_a: Immediately, at the time of signing
choice_b: Within 10 business days of signing
choice_c: At closing only
choice_d: Within 3 years, upon written request
explanation: Rule 3.2(A) requires a licensee to 'immediately (at the time of signing) deliver a true and correct copy of any instrument to any party or parties executing the same.' This duty is echoed as a statutory disciplinary ground: failing to voluntarily furnish such copies at signing is listed in Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-21(1)(i).
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Part 1601, Ch. 3, Rule 3.2(A); Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-21(1)(i)

question: Under Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-21, failing to voluntarily furnish, at the time of signing, copies of all listings, contracts, and agreements to all parties executing them is:
choice_a: A minor clerical matter with no licensing consequence
choice_b: Grounds for refusing to issue, suspending, or revoking a license
choice_c: Excused if the broker operates as a corporation rather than an individual
choice_d: Only a violation if a party complains in writing within 30 days
explanation: Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-21(1)(i) lists 'failing to furnish voluntarily, at the time of signing, copies of all listings, contracts and agreements to all parties executing the same' as one of the statutory grounds on which the Commission may refuse to issue, suspend, or revoke a real estate license. There is no exception for corporate licensees and no requirement that a party first file a complaint.
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-21(1)(i)

question: MREC's Rules and Regulations define a licensee's 'Work File' as:
choice_a: Only the fully executed sales contract
choice_b: Only documents the Commission specifically requests during an investigation
choice_c: Any and all documentation of a real estate transaction maintained by a licensee
choice_d: A file kept solely by the buyer's attorney
explanation: Rule 5.2(Z), within the Complaint Procedure chapter's definitions, defines 'Work File' broadly as 'any and all documentation of a real estate transaction maintained by a licensee,' and then lists (non-exhaustively) fourteen categories such as agency agreements, contracts of sale, closing documents, escrow records, listings, offers to purchase, and options.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Part 1601, Ch. 5, Rule 5.2(Z); Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-23, §73-35-25, §73-35-35

question: Which document is specifically listed as part of a licensee's 'Work File' under MREC Rule 5.2(Z)?
choice_a: The broker's personal federal tax return
choice_b: The listing agent's personal calendar
choice_c: A competitor's advertising brochure
choice_d: A Property Condition Disclosure Statement (PCDS), together with any Informational Statement or Seller's Statement of Exclusion
explanation: Rule 5.2(Z)(13) expressly includes 'Property Condition Disclosure Statements (PCDS), with Informational Statement or Seller's Statement of Exclusion, when applicable' within the definition of a licensee's Work File that must be maintained and, if requested during an investigation, produced to the Commission.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Part 1601, Ch. 5, Rule 5.2(Z)(13)

question: How does MREC Rule 5.2(Z) treat a Wood Destroying Insect Report (WDIR) obtained in connection with a transaction?
choice_a: It is listed within the 'Work File' definition as documentation the licensee maintains
choice_b: It is not considered part of the transaction file at all
choice_c: It is only required to be kept by the pest control company, not the broker
choice_d: It is only relevant to commercial, not residential, transactions
explanation: Rule 5.2(Z)(14) lists 'Wood Destroying Insect Reports (WDIR)' as one of the fourteen enumerated categories of documentation comprising a licensee's Work File, meaning it is a document the licensee is expected to maintain in the transaction file, not just a record held exclusively by the inspecting pest control company.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Part 1601, Ch. 5, Rule 5.2(Z)(14)

question: Per the MREC Work File definition in Rule 5.2(Z), what condition must a listing agreement satisfy to be considered valid?
choice_a: It must be witnessed by a notary public
choice_b: It must be in writing
choice_c: It must be recorded with the county chancery clerk
choice_d: It must be co-signed by the Commission's Administrator
explanation: Rule 5.2(Z)(10) lists 'Listing agreements, including extensions (must be in writing to be valid)' as part of the Work File, reinforcing the separate writing requirement for exclusive listing agreements found in Rule 3.2(B). Notarization, recording, and Commission co-signature are not required for a listing agreement's validity.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Part 1601, Ch. 5, Rule 5.2(Z)(10); Rule 3.2(B)

question: During a Commission investigation, within how many days must a licensee submit their entire work file, an Affidavit, and a written response to the allegations?
choice_a: 3 days
choice_b: 30 days
choice_c: 10 days
choice_d: 60 days
explanation: Rule 5.3(D) requires licensees to submit their entire work file/documentation of the real estate transaction at issue, together with an Affidavit and a written, notarized response to the allegations, within ten (10) days of the date of service of written notice upon the licensee and the licensee's Responsible Broker.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Part 1601, Ch. 5, Rule 5.3(D); Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-21, §73-35-23, §73-35-35

question: The Affidavit a licensee submits with their work file during an investigation must:
choice_a: Be signed only by the Responsible Broker, never the licensee
choice_b: Be filed only after the administrative hearing concludes
choice_c: Waive the licensee's right to legal counsel
choice_d: Certify that complete, accurate, and true copies of all documents germane to the transaction are being tendered, with a notarized signature
explanation: Rule 5.3(D)(1) requires the Affidavit to certify that complete, accurate, and true copies of all documents germane to the real estate transaction under investigation are being tendered to the Commission, and requires the licensee's signature to be notarized. It does not need to be signed exclusively by the Responsible Broker, filed post-hearing, or serve as a waiver of counsel.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Part 1601, Ch. 5, Rule 5.3(D)(1)

question: Under Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-23, the Commission is authorized and empowered to:
choice_a: Issue subpoenas for the attendance of witnesses and the production of books and papers, statewide
choice_b: Issue subpoenas only for witness testimony, never for documents
choice_c: Seize a broker's office equipment without notice
choice_d: Compel testimony only from licensed attorneys
explanation: Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-23(3) authorizes the Commission 'to issue subpoenas for the attendance of witnesses and the production of books and papers,' with process extending 'to all parts of the state.' This document-production power is distinct from any right to seize property outright.
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-23(3)

question: If a witness in a Commission proceeding refuses to produce books and papers called for by a Commission subpoena, what happens under §73-35-23?
choice_a: The Commission has no recourse and must drop the matter
choice_b: A court of competent jurisdiction may enforce production in the same manner as in civil cases
choice_c: The refusal is automatically treated as an admission of guilt
choice_d: The witness is fined directly by the Commission without judicial involvement
explanation: Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-23(4) provides that where a witness fails or refuses to attend upon a Commission subpoena, testify, or produce subpoenaed books and papers, 'the attendance of such witness and the giving of his testimony and the production of the books and papers shall be enforced by any court of competent jurisdiction of this state in the same manner as ... in civil cases.'
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-23(4)

question: MREC Rule 3.4(C) requires that escrow account records be kept:
choice_a: In any format the broker prefers, with no accounting standard specified
choice_b: Only in a single consolidated account for all clients, undifferentiated
choice_c: In accordance with standard accounting practices, with all monies individually identified as to a particular transaction
choice_d: By the buyer's lender, not the broker
explanation: Rule 3.4(C) requires accurate records of all monies received, disbursed, or on hand in escrow, with all monies 'individually identified as to a particular transaction' and kept 'in accordance with standard accounting practices' -- not commingled into one undifferentiated account, and not delegated to the lender.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Part 1601, Ch. 3, Rule 3.4(C)

question: Under Rule 3.2(B), an exclusive listing agreement must include all of the following EXCEPT:
choice_a: The sales price and considerations to be paid
choice_b: Signatures of all parties to the agreement
choice_c: A definite date of expiration
choice_d: The broker's personal home address
explanation: Rule 3.2(B) requires exclusive listing agreements to be in writing, properly identify the property, and contain the sales price, considerations to be paid, signatures of all parties, and a definite date of expiration. It does not require the broker's personal home address to appear in the agreement.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Part 1601, Ch. 3, Rule 3.2(B)

question: Rule 3.2(C) imposes similar written-document requirements on which type of agreement?
choice_a: Exclusive buyer representation agreements
choice_b: Property management agreements only
choice_c: Verbal open-house sign-in sheets
choice_d: Advertising contracts with newspapers
explanation: Rule 3.2(C) requires exclusive buyer representation agreements to be in writing and to properly identify the terms and conditions under which the buyer will rely on the broker for the purchase of real estate, including the price range acceptable to the buyer, considerations to be paid, signatures of all parties, and a definite date of expiration.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Part 1601, Ch. 3, Rule 3.2(C)

question: When an offer is made on listed property, Rule 3.2(H) requires the broker to:
choice_a: Immediately reject any offer below the listing price
choice_b: Document and date the seller's personal acceptance or rejection of the offer, and provide a copy to the offering party upon written request
choice_c: Destroy the offer once a decision is communicated verbally
choice_d: Forward the offer only to the seller's attorney, never to the seller directly
explanation: Rule 3.2(H) requires that when an offer is made on property under a listing agreement, the broker 'shall document and date the seller's personal acceptance or rejection of the offer and upon written request, shall provide a copy of such document to the person making the offer.' There is no rule requiring automatic rejection of below-price offers or routing exclusively through an attorney.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Part 1601, Ch. 3, Rule 3.2(H)

question: Under Rule 3.1(F), what is the consequence if a licensee fails, in a timely manner, to respond to official MREC written communication?
choice_a: No consequence unless the failure is repeated three times
choice_b: The Commission must first refer the matter to the Attorney General for a criminal charge
choice_c: The licensee is deemed, prima facie, guilty of improper dealing
choice_d: The broker's errors and omissions insurance is automatically cancelled
explanation: Rule 3.1(F) provides that any licensee who fails, in a timely manner, to respond to official Mississippi Real Estate Commission written communication, or who fails or neglects to abide by the Commission's Rules and Regulations, 'shall be deemed, prima facie, to be guilty of improper dealing.' A single failure to respond triggers this presumption; no repeat-offense threshold or prior criminal referral is required.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Part 1601, Ch. 3, Rule 3.1(F)

question: Under Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-5(4), records kept in the office of the Mississippi Real Estate Commission are:
choice_a: Permanently confidential and never subject to inspection
choice_b: Available only to licensed attorneys
choice_c: Automatically destroyed after two years
choice_d: Open to public inspection, except pending investigative files
explanation: Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-5(4) provides that 'all records kept in the office of the commission under the authority of this chapter shall be open to public inspection except pending investigative files.' This governs the Commission's own official records (distinct from a broker's private transaction files, which are subject to the separate three-year retention and Commission-audit rules).
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-5(4)

question: A Mississippi broker who repeatedly fails to maintain required transaction records, resulting in a finding of dishonest or improper dealing, faces which range of consequences under Mississippi law?
choice_a: License refusal, suspension, or revocation under §73-35-21, and potentially criminal fines or imprisonment under §73-35-31
choice_b: Only a private letter of reprimand, with no other options available
choice_c: Automatic revocation of the license of every other licensee in the state
choice_d: Loss of errors and omissions coverage only, with no licensing action possible
explanation: Recordkeeping failures rising to the level of bad faith, incompetency, untrustworthiness, or dishonest, fraudulent, or improper dealing fall under the catch-all disciplinary ground in Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-21(1)(n), exposing the broker to license refusal, suspension, or revocation. Separately, §73-35-31 imposes criminal fines (and, for repeat violations, possible imprisonment) for violations of the License Law chapter, independent of any Commission disciplinary action.
